title: Split-quaternionic structure and canonical quantization of the Bateman dual oscillator
abstract: Bateman's dual oscillator embeds a damped harmonic oscillator and an independent anti-damped adjoint coordinate in a conservative doubled system. We develop a split-quaternionic formulation that remains consistent from the classical equations through ordinary complex canonical quantization. The doubled dynamics is written as a two-sided hypercomplex evolution whose conserved indefinite quadratic form is the split norm, while the sign of the generator square unifies the underdamped, overdamped, and critical regimes. The Bateman Lagrangian is recovered as a real scalar action on the split-complex configuration subalgebra. After quantization, operator-valued split quaternions belong to the complexified algebra $\mathbb C\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb H_s\simeq M_2(\mathbb C)$. Noncommuting mechanical components require a symmetrized quantum split norm, which exactly reproduces the symmetrically ordered canonical Hamiltonian. Null idempotents resolve the crossed canonical structure of the doubled phase space. In particular, damping yields $[m\dot{\widehat y},m\dot{\widehat x}]=\mathrm{i}\hbar mγ$ and a Robertson--Schrödinger uncertainty relation. The limit $γ\to0$ retains the doubled positive/negative geometry; the ordinary single-oscillator Heisenberg relation is recovered only after selecting the positive normal mode, or by undoubling before quantization. The scalar split action gives the exact quadratic propagator and Gaussian evolution. A formal trace over the auxiliary coordinate is finally compared with high-temperature Caldeira--Leggett dynamics, clarifying that the doubled model is a coherent zero-noise embedding rather than a microscopic reservoir theory.
summary: This paper quantizes the Bateman dual oscillator using an advanced split-quaternionic algebraic structure. It successfully derives the system's propagator and shows that this mathematical framework describes a reversible, zero-noise embedding of damping. Crucially, it distinguishes its approach from standard open quantum system theories like Caldeira–Leggett by analyzing the resulting reduced density matrix.
main_problem: The paper develops a unified algebraic framework using split-quaternionic structures to canonically quantize the Bateman dual oscillator, which models damped harmonic motion.
main_result: The formulation successfully provides an exact quadratic propagator and Gaussian evolution for the doubled system, clarifying that it represents a coherent zero-noise embedding rather than a true microscopic reservoir theory.
method: The authors employ split-quaternionic algebra to construct operator-valued generalizations of the dynamics on the doubled phase space, leading to canonical quantization rules.
model_or_system: The system is the Bateman dual oscillator, which couples a damped harmonic oscillator with an independent anti-damped adjoint coordinate. The analysis extends this classical model into a quantum domain using hypercomplex algebra.
key_observables: Robertson–Schrödinger uncertainty relation; reduced position density $ho_{SQ}(x, t)$; the propagator $K(q_f, q_i; t)$.
important_parameters: Damping coefficient ($\gamma$), natural frequency ($\omega_0$), and Planck's constant ($\hbar$).
main_assumptions: The comparison with Caldeira–Leggett dynamics assumes the doubled model is a coherent embedding, not a standard bath coupling; the recovery of single-oscillator relations requires selecting only one normal mode.
figures_summary: Figures compare the reduced position variance ($	ext{xx}(t)$) for both the split-quaternionic and Caldeira–Leggett models, showing saturation versus diffusive growth.
paper_structure: The paper systematically develops the classical dynamics via Lagrangian reduction to known damped forms, then introduces the split-quaternionic quantization framework. It calculates the quantum propagator and finally contrasts the resulting reduced density matrix with standard open system descriptions like Caldeira–Leggett theory.
why_interesting: It provides a novel mathematical tool (split-quaternions) to handle non-Hermitian or doubled dynamics in quantum mechanics, offering insights into how damping can be treated symmetrically without invoking explicit environmental coupling.
